'''Squadron Members''' (often abbreviated '''SM''') were Decipher's volunteer local promoters for ''Star Wars'' CCG in the 1990s: they hosted tournaments, ran demos, and helped players. [[Ming Huo]] (mingtown) described them as volunteers who helped Decipher coordinate events.

Decipher organized them as Gold, Red, Bravo, and Rogue squadrons, with Leaders usually listed at Decipher Inc. The published lists are a GeoCities fan transcription (''Corellian Engineering Corporation'' / plarathas) later reprinted by the [[Players Committee]] (1 July 2021) as "the original list of Squadron Members."

This wiki keeps the list as '''history'''. Towns are as published. Vacant numbered slots are printed "-----" as on the PC reprint. Obvious typing errors on the GeoCities/PC HTML (for example Virgina, Elletsville, Mithc, An=rendain) are repaired in the person titles; the original strings remain on the source pages.

The GeoCities page also asked Squadron Members to help complete a set of black-border signed X-wings, Y-wings, Snowspeeders, and Naboo Starfighters.

== Flight Leaders ==

'''FL''' on the published Gold, Red, Bravo, and Rogue tables stands for '''Flight Leader''', per [[Ming Huo]] (mingtown) and [[Scott Lingrell]].

[[Scott Lingrell]] said Flight Leaders were a step up from a normal volunteer: "It wasn't really ranked higher, but they were just key volunteers that would be more involved directly with Decipher."

== How the lists survive ==

* Original GeoCities path: <code>geocities.com/plarathas/</code> and <code>geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/</code> (same site; last homepage note on the later mirrors is 15 August 2005, GenCon / SWCCG Worlds in Indianapolis).
* Wayback of the '''original''' GeoCities home: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010513005725/http://www.geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/ 13 May 2001] (HTTP 200; further 200 captures 17 May, 26 May, 21 July 2001). The 13 May 2001 page already links [[Anagrams|anagrams.html]], names [[John Sarnecki]] as the former Squadron Member who started King of Corellia, and lists TDs [[Alex Alcalde]] (Gold 31), [[John Kaufeld]], and [[Craig Spaid]] (Bravo 36).
* Wayback of <code>geocities.com/plarathas/SMs.html</code>: [https://web.archive.org/web/20091028130457/http://geocities.com/plarathas/SMs.html 28 October 2009] is HTTP 410 (Yahoo had already shut GeoCities).
* Live mirrors: [https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/SMs.html geocities.ws] · [https://www.oocities.org/collegepark/plaza/9433/ oocities.org] (oocities home/anagrams also on Wayback from 2019).
* Reocities copy used by Encyclopedia 3.2 for [[Anagrams]] ([https://web.archive.org/web/20160406045459/http://www.reocities.com/CollegePark/plaza/9433/anagrams.html Wayback 6 April 2016]; earlier captures 9 May 2014 and 20 February 2016).
* Reocities copy of SMs.html: [https://web.archive.org/web/20160409152825/http://reocities.com/collegepark/plaza/9433/SMs.html Wayback 9 April 2016] (HTTP 200; same roster as the PC reprint).
* PC reprint (1 July 2021): [https://www.starwarsccg.org/decipher-swccg-squadron-members/ Decipher SWCCG Squadron Members] ("This is the original list of Squadron Members."). Same names as GeoCities; see [[#PC reprint vs GeoCities]] for the small differences.


== PC reprint vs GeoCities ==

The [https://www.starwarsccg.org/decipher-swccg-squadron-members/ Players Committee page] is the same roster as GeoCities, not a different list. Differences:

* The PC table has no Status column. GeoCities marked almost every filled slot '''Retired''' (the program ended with the printed game) and noted a few moves: [[Kyle Heuer]] Red 7 &rarr; Rogue Leader; [[Kevin Ch'ng]] Red 17 &rarr; Gold 13; [[Francis Lalumiere]] Red 23 &rarr; Gold 28; [[Guillermo Ruiz]] Gold 17 &rarr; Red 42. Those people still appear in both squadrons on both lists. This wiki omits Retired; the four moves are the only status facts worth keeping, and they are already visible as duplicate listings.
* Red 3 is [[Jason Robinette]] on the PC page and "Jason R" on GeoCities (truncated). This wiki follows the PC name.
* Red Leader is spelled '''Jonathon''' on both published tables; this wiki uses [[Jonathan Quesenberry]] (with a redirect from Jonathon).
* GeoCities/PC share the same typos (Virgina, Gainsville, Hungry, Joel An=rendain, Mithc, etc.). This wiki repairs those in titles.
* Both lists include the same vacant slots (Gold 10, 21&ndash;23, 25&ndash;26, 99&ndash;100; Red 9, 28&ndash;29, 75&ndash;76, 120; Bravo 22).

== Completeness of the published lists ==

The GeoCities tribute called itself a complete list of Red, Gold, Rogue, and Bravo Squadron Members. [[Scott Lingrell]] said that list is incomplete. He was Rogue 60. He first recalled the slot as Gold 60; the published Gold 60 is [[Dave Chapman]] of Sumter, SC. Those Rogue tables end at Rogue 40 ([[Doug Faust]], Ithaca, NY).

== First Players' Committee advocates (January 2002) ==

Warren Holland's 25 January 2002 announcement named six Player Advocates. Several were already Squadron Members:

* [[Michael Girard]] — Player Support (Gold 120)
* [[John Arendt]] — Tournament Support (Bravo 16)
* [[Joe Helfrich]] and [[Greg Anderson]] — Rules Support (Bravo 15 / Rogue 31)
* [[Eric Olson]] and [[Doug Taylor]] — Gameplay Support (Bravo 7 / Red 4 FL)

Holland wrote that the committee would become a new Product Champion Squadron working beside the existing squadrons, and that GamePlayers Network would help with web tools and prize shipping after 30 April 2002.
